business_scope.primary_industry_name: Digital Intermediary for Regulated Startup Equity Offerings

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (Hong Kong SAR)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA) and its Investment Agreement

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) of the laws of Hong Kong SAR, including sections 67 (incorporation application), 101 (statement of capital), 112 (registered office), 113 (appointment of initial directors), 114 (minimum director qualifications), 127 (company secretary), 135 (register of members), 139 (allotment of shares), 659 (registered office change notices), and 716 (minutes); Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), section 6; Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571), section 114 (Type 1 regulated activity); Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615), Schedule 2. The group taxonomy 'WFOE' is an internal label; the legal vehicle is a private company limited by shares in Hong Kong.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR (Integrated Company Registry Information System, ICRIS) and the One-Stop Company and Commercial Registration Office, 14/F, Queensway Government Offices, 66 Queensway, Hong Kong
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Form NNC1 (Application for Incorporation of a Company Limited by Shares), together with the Articles of Association and consent forms of the initial director(s), company secretary, and registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow capital account. The company may issue a single ordinary share of HKD 1.00 (approximately USD 0.13) at incorporation. The Articles of Association may authorize further share capital, and all allotments must comply with the statement of capital and return of allotment filing obligations under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CN WFOE LTD (the 'Company')

At a first meeting of the board of directors of the Company duly convened at the registered office on [Date] at [Time] (Hong Kong time), with all first directors present in person and by electronic communication as permitted by the Articles of Association and the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), the chairperson declared the meeting quorate and the following resolutions were put to the board, seconded, deliberated, and adopted unanimously:

1. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, that the initial issued share capital of the Company be and is hereby fixed at HKD 1.00 divided into 1 ordinary share of HKD 1.00 par value; that the subscription of such share by the sole shareholder be and is hereby approved; and that the directors be and are hereby authorized to issue, allot, and enter the share into the register of members, to apply any share premium, to declare the statement of capital, and to file the return of allotment with the Companies Registry as required by law.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby established at the address stated in the Incorporation Form NNC1, and that the directors be and are hereby authorized to maintain the registered office, amend the Articles as required, and notify the Companies Registry of any change of the registered office under section 659.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that [Bank Name] and such other banks as the board may select be and are hereby designated as the Company's bankers; that the directors, together with the company secretary or any two directors, be and are hereby authorized to open such accounts, sign such mandates, receive deposits, execute checks, accept escrow instructions, and establish ACH and wire transfer facilities as may be necessary for the equity crowdfunding platform; and that all banking operations comply with applicable anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing obligations.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that [Director One] be and is hereby appointed Managing Director, [Director Two] be and is hereby appointed Compliance Officer, and [Secretary Firm] be and is hereby appointed Company Secretary, each to serve with full authority to execute statutory returns, sign contracts, and correspond with the Companies Registry, the Inland Revenue Department, and the Securities and Futures Commission on behalf of the Company.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that any two directors, or one director and the company secretary, be and are hereby authorized to execute all documents, to pay the relevant filing fees and duties, to appoint legal counsel and auditors, and to do all things necessary to implement these resolutions lawfully and to procure the SFC licence and other regulatory permits required for the equity crowdfunding portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name search and incorporation submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) and e-Registry portal; One-Stop Company and Commercial Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search in the ICRIS database to ensure the proposed company name is not prohibited, illegal, or too similar to an existing Hong Kong name. Obtain the written consent of the owner of the proposed registered office. Complete and sign Form NNC1 and the Articles of Association, and pay the incorporation fee. The application must state the initial director(s), company secretary, statement of capital, and registered office address. If the sole shareholder is a foreign corporation, attach a certified copy of its certificate of incorporation, a board resolution authorizing the subscription, and, if the executing officer signs outside Hong Kong, a notarially certified or apostilled execution page. Submit the package via the e-Registry portal or in person at the One-Stop office.
required_dossiers: Completed Form NNC1
Articles of Association signed by all subscribers
Consent to act of first director(s) and company secretary
Consent to use registered office address
Certified copy of the foreign corporate shareholder's certificate of incorporation
Board resolution of the foreign corporate shareholder authorizing the incorporation
Notarially certified or apostilled execution page if signed outside Hong Kong
Proof of incorporation fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry issues a query, requisition, or suspension, respond in writing within the specified period, not exceeding 14 days, with corrected documents. If the objection is to the company name, submit a fresh name application under section 100. If the objection relates to subscriber authority, provide the original or notarially certified board resolution and power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration and tax account activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office, One-Stop Company and Commercial Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after the date of incorporation, apply for a Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310). Complete Form IRBR1 and pay the prescribed business registration fee and levy. The application can be submitted online through the Government's eTAX portal or together with the incorporation application using the One-Stop service. The Business Registration Certificate states the company's business name and address and is a mandatory condition for opening bank accounts, executing commercial contracts, and applying to the Securities and Futures Commission. If the company operates a separate trade name, also apply for a Branch Business Registration Certificate. Retain the certificate for display at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Form NNC1 acknowledgment
Identity cards or passports of the directors and company secretary
Proof of registered office address
Completed Form IRBR1
Payment receipt for business registration fee and levy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Inland Revenue Department raises a query on the business registration application, correct the application on eTAX within 14 days. If the Business Registration Certificate is delayed, use the IRD acknowledgment for bank account opening. If a late filing penalty arises, submit a written mitigation request with evidence of exceptional circumstances and pay the required penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting, statutory books, and share allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's registered office, the appointed company secretary, and the Companies Registry for subsequent statutory filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene and minute a first board meeting at which the pro-forma board resolution is adopted. Approve the issue of the initial HKD 1 share, enter the subscriber in the register of members, and issue a share certificate. Record the directors' service contracts, the company secretary's certificate of consent, and the registered office location in the statutory books. Appoint external auditors, adopt a corporate seal or electronic signing policy, and ensure the statutory records are kept at the registered office or at an alternative approved location in Hong Kong. If necessary, file a return of allotment and any change of director or secretary form with the Companies Registry within the statutory period.
required_dossiers: Incorporation certificate
First board meeting minutes and resolutions
Register of members and share certificate
Consent to act certificates
Statutory books and records
Auditor appointment letter
Return of allotment form (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the statutory period for filing forms has passed, pay the prescribed late filing fee and file through the e-Registry. If the registered office consent is contested, execute a notice of change of registered office on Form NR1 promptly. Rectify a missing company secretary consent by obtaining a signed consent form and filing the necessary notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Securities and Futures Commission licence application for equity crowdfunding portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), Licensing and Internet Governance Department; Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau for policy context; Companies Registry for prospectus registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the portal will arrange or deal in equity securities, apply to the SFC for a corporation licence carrying on the regulated activity of dealing in securities (Type 1) under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571). Prepare a comprehensive business plan covering the crowdfunding platform, client escrow arrangements, risk warnings, due diligence processes, and compliance controls. Appoint at least two responsible officers who are fit and proper and submit their individual licence declarations. Implement robust anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing policies, cyber security controls, and client money segregation procedures. If the equity offer will reach the Hong Kong public, address the prospectus registration or exemption requirements under the Companies (Winding Up and Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance. Submit all forms and annexes through the SFC licensing portal, pay the licence fee, and maintain ongoing notification duties.
required_dossiers: SFC prescribed corporate licence application forms
Responsible officer application forms and personal declarations
Detailed business plan and platform operating model
Anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing policies
Client money and escrow handling procedures
Risk management and cybersecurity compliance manual
Certified copies of Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Association
Fit and proper declarations for directors and responsible officers
Bank references and financial standing evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SFC raises questions or rejects the application, respond by the stated deadline with additional compliance evidence, amend the business plan, or replace non-fit-and-proper officers and resubmit the application. If refusal is issued, consider an appeal to the Securities and Futures Appeals Tribunal under the SFO or submit a fresh application after remediation. In the interim, do not operate the crowdfunding platform without a licence or an applicable exemption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental and fire safety applicability check for digital intermediary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Environmental Protection Department, Fire Services Department, and Labour Department, solely for verification and record purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Classify the company under ISIC 6499 as a digital financial intermediary with no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehouse activities. Document this classification in an internal compliance memorandum and align the business plan with the SFC application. Confirm that the office lease and premises are used solely for administrative and platform operations, and maintain any Fire Service Installation and Equipment Certificate required by the lease or the Buildings Ordinance. Should the company later acquire physical facilities, prior approval under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499), the Fire Services Ordinance (Cap. 95), and the Occupational Safety and Occupational Health Ordinance (Cap. 509) would become mandatory. Update this assessment annually.
required_dossiers: Compliance memorandum confirming no physical industrial operations
Office lease and premise usage confirmation
Fire Service Installation and Equipment Certificate if required
No industrial activity declaration signed by the director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Environmental Protection Department or Fire Services Department questions the classification or discovers unapproved physical operations, cease the affected activity immediately, engage a professional consultant, and apply for the required environmental, fire safety, and occupational health permits. Submit a remedial compliance plan to the relevant authorities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for industrial or physical permitting. ISIC 6499 is a non-industrial financial intermediary service. No physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing operation is licenced under the Factory and Industrial Undertakings Ordinance (Cap. 59).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable for an industrial operating permit. The operative authorization for the equity crowdfunding portal is a Securities and Futures Commission licence for Type 1 regulated activity, dealing in securities, under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571), together with any Business Registration Certificate under Cap. 310.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department (EPD), Hong Kong SAR
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable. No Schedule 2 designated project under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499). Digital portal operations generate no point-source wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. No registered effluent discharge under the Water Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 358), no specified processes under the Air Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 311), and no chemical waste producer registration under the Waste Disposal Ordinance (Cap. 354). Office waste and electronic waste, if generated, must be handled through licensed collectors or recyclers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for factory or warehouse fire-load categories under the Fire Services Ordinance (Cap. 95). The office premises must maintain any required Fire Service Installation and Equipment Certificate under the Buildings Ordinance and the lease, and must comply with workplace safety obligations under the Occupational Safety and Occupational Health Ordinance (Cap. 509).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) for the mainland China WFOE; official online portal: www.chinatax.gov.cn and the STA Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) platform. For the Hong Kong SAR parent or offshore profits, the competent authority is the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region with the eTAX portal at www.ird.gov.hk.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign investor must first register the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) with the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR), complete foreign investment information reporting under the MOFCOM negative-list framework, and obtain a business license containing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). The WFOE must then complete tax registration with the STA within 30 calendar days via the e-Tax bureau or the local tax service hall. The USCC is the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number. The WFOE must complete real-name authentication, bank-account linking for tax payment, and VAT general taxpayer qualification if annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000 or if its business model requires input VAT crediting. Supporting documents include the articles of association, legal representative identity proof, registered office lease, evidence of paid-in capital remittance, and bank account registration. A foreign non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment that derives China-source income obtains a non-resident tax registration or is administered through a withholding agent in accordance with the STA non-resident tax administration framework.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope applies to the Hong Kong SAR parent because Hong Kong profits tax is territorial, but the mainland China WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise subject to entity-level Corporate Income Tax at 25%, VAT, urban maintenance and construction tax, and education surcharges. The WFOE is not a pass-through entity and has no tax-transparent classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: China does not provide a check-the-box election. The WFOE may elect small-scale VAT taxpayer treatment while annual taxable sales remain below RMB 5,000,000; once it registers as a general VAT taxpayer, the election is irrevocable and the normal VAT credit-offset method applies. Small-scale taxpayers may apply simplified levy rates under STA temporary relief measures. Hong Kong SAR does not have a check-the-box regime; territorial source rules are non-elective, and no hybrid mismatch election is available under PRC domestic tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China. Hong Kong SAR does not impose VAT, GST, or state-level sales tax; it applies excise duties, stamp duty, and profits tax instead.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales: annual sales above this threshold require compulsory VAT general taxpayer registration. All WFOEs must complete statutory tax registration within 30 days of business license issuance; below the threshold the entity may remain a small-scale VAT taxpayer. Hong Kong SAR has no VAT/GST registration threshold because no such tax exists.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mainland China enforces real-time e-invoice clearance through the STA VAT Invoice Management System and the Full Digital Electronic Invoice Platform (all-electronic invoice). Taxpayers must issue Special VAT Invoices or digital e-invoices through the STA platform and upload transactional data in real time under the Golden Tax Phase IV architecture, with API integration for enterprise billing systems. Anti-fraud digital stamping uses unique invoice codes, encrypted invoice numbering, taxpayer real-name authentication, and automated cross-matching of VAT invoices. Hong Kong SAR imposes no electronic invoicing or fiscal clearance mandate because it operates no VAT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the PRC VAT export tax rebate framework, goods physically exported from China may obtain a 0% VAT rate or exemption/rebate if the export is declared by the registered VAT taxpayer in its own name and the foreign exchange receipt is repatriated through designated banks. Cross-border services may qualify for zero-rating or VAT exemption under Cai Shui [2016] No. 36 and implementing STA rules only where the recipient is outside China, the service is wholly consumed outside China, and the consideration is paid in foreign currency from outside China. An equity crowdfunding portal's facilitation fees are generally taxable at 6% as financial or direct charging intermediary services; zero-rating is not automatic and will apply only if the WFOE can prove a qualifying offshore digital service transaction, offshore recipient, offshore actual consumption, and timely foreign-exchange repatriation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export goods declaration) bearing the China Customs release serial number and the exporter's customs registration code
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical export from China
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign-exchange settlement record from a designated SAFE bank proving repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days
Commercial invoice, export sales contract, and packing list connecting the transaction to the exporting WFOE
PRC VAT export invoice or special VAT invoice and the export tax rebate application filed with the STA
For zero-rated cross-border services: offshore service contract, proof of offshore recipient and offshore consumption, and proof of foreign-currency settlement from outside China
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: China Customs and the STA jointly audit export declarations, logistics documents, foreign-exchange receipts, and VAT credit flows. Failure to substantiate zero-rating is treated as fraudulent export tax rebate or false zero-rated declaration. The STA will claw back refunded VAT, impose a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day from the due date, and impose an administrative fine of one to five times the tax amount fraudulently obtained under the Law on Administration of Tax Levy and Collection. The WFOE's export tax credit classification will be downgraded, zero-rating and export rebate privileges will be suspended, and the case may be transferred for criminal prosecution under the Criminal Law where the false declaration amount is significant. Records must be retained and made available to the STA for audit; failure to repatriate foreign currency within the 180-day deadline or falsification of offshore consumption will result in retroactive re-taxation at the standard VAT rate, clawback of input VAT refunds, and withholding tax assessments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) as the central bank, acting jointly with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE); the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is the de facto central bank and monetary authority for the Hong Kong SAR leg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The WFOE operates under China's controlled convertibility framework. RMB is convertible for current account transactions such as merchandise trade, service payments, royalties, dividends on foreign direct investment, and reasonable operating expenses, but capital account transactions, including inbound equity injections, shareholder loans, and overseas direct investment, require mandatory SAFE registration and bank-level authenticity verification. In Hong Kong, the HKMA maintains the linked exchange rate system with free capital and current account convertibility, so the HK parent treasury can transfer equity capital into the Chinese WFOE without FX restriction. The WFOE's inbound foreign currency capital contribution must be credited to a SAFE-monitored FX capital account, and the bank will require the underlying foreign investment filing, the equity subscription agreement, and a post-receipt capital verification report from a Chinese certified public accountant. Profit remittances to the Hong Kong shareholder are permitted only after the WFOE completes its annual audit, corporate income tax settlement, and withholding tax filing; under the Mainland-Hong Kong double taxation arrangement, dividends may qualify for a reduced 5% withholding tax if Hong Kong is the ultimate beneficial owner. The convertibility gap is therefore structural rather than transactional: operating flows are freely convertible, while capital movements remain tightly controlled and require a paper trail that the corporate treasury must maintain for regulatory inspections.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's current account administration, there is no mandatory surrender ratio. Export proceeds in foreign currency may be retained in full in an onshore FX current-account bank account or voluntarily converted into RMB through the bank's settlement system. The statutory repatriation window for export receipts is 180 days from the customs declaration date unless the exporter obtains prior SAFE approval for offshore retention. Every receipt must be reported through the SAFE Trade Monitoring System, and the bank performs documentary reconciliation against bills of lading, customs declarations, and invoices.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Settlement Account (RMB) and Foreign Currency Capital Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account with RMB and USD sub-ledgers
Capital Escrow Account for inbound equity injection and domestic operating settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable for the WFOE. PBOC and the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission restrict onshore deposit-taking, FX settlement, and cross-border RMB transactions to licensed commercial banks. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, and Airwallex cannot hold WFOE capital, custody client escrow funds, or issue RMB settlement accounts in mainland China. They may only serve the Hong Kong parent for ancillary multicurrency treasury activity outside China, but the WFOE must maintain all onshore accounts at a licensed PRC commercial bank. Feasibility rating: Low.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory legal representative of the WFOE must normally appear physically at the bank branch for the account-opening interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for a new WFOE account. If the director resides in Hong Kong, the bank may accept a notarized and apostilled power of attorney appointing a local authorized signatory, provided the director completes a two-way video interview with the bank compliance officer. Final approval requires the bank's branch-level Anti-Money Laundering Committee to approve the documentary package and the equity crowdfunding business risk profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disguised beneficial ownership through the Hong Kong parent and layered crowdfunding investors obscures the ultimate owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of Hong Kong Business Registration certificate and Certificate of Incorporation; register of directors; register of members reflecting all shareholders above 5% ownership; ultimate beneficial owner attestation covering every natural person holding 25% or more of each layer; written explanation of any bearer shares, nominee holdings, or trustee structures; bank reference letters; notarized passports of all shareholders above 10%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High inherent money laundering risk from an equity crowdfunding portal that pools investor funds and may mix client money with operating treasury.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid statutory license for equity crowdfunding or equivalent financial regulatory approval; escrow and client money segregation agreement with a licensed third-party bank or payment institution; fully audited settlement ledger; treasury policy showing legal separation of investor escrow balances from operating funds; copy of the internal control manual; annual external audit report; explicit statement of no anonymous investor participation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable source of wealth for inbound foreign equity capital arriving from Hong Kong shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: For each subscribing shareholder, 12 months of bank statements, audited financial statements, tax returns, wealth origin questionnaire, and a signed source-of-funds deed confirming no proceeds of crime, tax evasion, or sanctions-related activity; corporate registry extract from Hong Kong Companies Registry; evidence of the economic substance of the HK treasury parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure and politically exposed person risk because an internet-based crowdfunding platform can attract investors across multiple high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening report against United Nations, OFAC, EU, and PRC consolidated lists for every shareholder, director, and beneficial owner; PEP screening questionnaire and adverse media search; jurisdiction risk scoring methodology; transaction monitoring and name-screening architecture description; suspicious transaction reporting escalation pack.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Hong Kong parent must initiate a SWIFT MT103 wire from its licensed Hong Kong bank to the WFOE's licensed PRC bank, crediting the SAFE-monitored FX capital account. The remitter must include the SAFE inbound foreign direct investment purpose code for equity injection, the foreign investment filing number, and the WFOE's enterprise registration number. Upon receipt, the PRC bank reports the transaction to SAFE's cross-border receipt reporting system, performs the underlying-contract authenticity check, and the WFOE must engage a Chinese certified public accountant to issue a capital verification report confirming the equity subscription. The incoming USD may then be converted into RMB through the bank's onshore FX system and used only for the WFOE's approved operating business and crowdfunding platform disbursements, subject to subsequent SAFE expenditure monitoring.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For domestic settlement of platform obligations, startup disbursements, and operating expenses, the WFOE should use China National Advanced Payment System clearing with ACH escrow instructions from its RMB settlement account; for time-critical vendor payments, SWIFT MT103 bank wire can be used. Cross-border disbursements to overseas beneficiaries must be supported by genuine underlying service, trade, or investment contracts, and any overseas equity investment must obtain SAFE overseas direct investment registration before the wire is released. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are permissible only for actual trade flows; they are secondary to the equity crowdfunding model, whose core agreed payment rails are escrow-held ACH settlement and bank wire.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/USD forward contracts and FX swaps executed with the PRC settlement bank solely to hedge genuinely forecasted current account receipts or approved capital account commitments, with zero speculative leverage and full underlying documentation.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permissible for the Hong Kong parent treasury center to hedge RMB exposure without delivering RMB, provided the WFOE does not create an onshore settlement obligation that would require SAFE approval.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps are permitted only when matched to long-term cross-border debt or capital financing structures, with the PRC bank's derivatives desk verifying SAFE registration, real economic exposure, and no embedded leverage beyond the underlying loan or investment contract.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form NAR1) for a Hong Kong Private Limited Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee escalates from HK$870 to HK$1,740 to HK$3,480 depending on the number of months overdue; continued default may result in prosecution and eventual strike-off of the company at the Companies Registry's discretion under Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month of the expiry date stated on the current Business Registration Certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Continuing without a valid business registration carries liability to a fine of up to HK$5,000 and imprisonment; repeated non-renewal may also trigger coercive recovery action by the Inland Revenue Department and criminal prosecution under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (Form BIR51) accompanied by Audited Financial Statements and Tax Computations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the issue date of the return, subject to extension for e-filing through a tax representative; the actual deadline is printed on each return and the IRD's annual issuance schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without reasonable excuse attracts penalties up to three times the amount of tax undercharged, additional fines, estimated assessments, and prosecution under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (Form BIR56A) and Annual Employee Remuneration Statements (IR56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the date of issue, normally issued in April after the tax year ending 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the Employer's Return and IR56B statements is an offence; the maximum penalty is HK$10,000 per omission and, where there is intent to evade tax, further penal liabilities including imprisonment under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Significant Controllers Register Annual Maintenance and On-Site Verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained at the company's registered office; no public filing to Companies Registry is required, but the register must be available for inspection by law enforcement authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Rolling obligation; the register must be updated within 7 calendar days of any change in a significant controller's particulars, and an annual internal review is recommended on the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the Significant Controllers Register regime under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) is an offence subject to a Level 5 fine of HK$50,000 and, in the case of continuing default, an additional daily fine of up to HK$1,000; directors and responsible officers are personally liable.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Every Hong Kong private limited company must be audited by a certified public accountant unless it qualifies for the small private company audit exemption under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). The qualifying conditions are satisfied when a small private company meets at least two of the three tests in a financial year: total annual revenue not exceeding HK$10,000,000; total assets not exceeding HK$10,000,000; and average number of employees not exceeding 50. However, this exemption is unavailable to the present entity because it holds a statutory license as a high-risk equity crowdfunding portal and is regulated under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571) and anti-money laundering legislation; therefore a compulsory independent certified CPA audit is mandatory regardless of turnover, balance sheet size, or headcount. The audit must be conducted in accordance with Hong Kong Standards on Auditing by a CPA firm under the Professional Accountants Ordinance (Cap. 50).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), which converge with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); the Hong Kong Small and Medium-Sized Entity Financial Reporting Standard (HK SME-FRS) is unavailable to a licensed financial intermediary with public accountability.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong imposes no public annual UBO filing. The company must maintain a Significant Controllers Register at its registered office under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), using reasonable steps to identify registrable persons, and must update the register as soon as reasonably practicable after any change, in any event within 7 calendar days. The Annual Return (NAR1) confirms member, director, and secretary particulars but does not contain UBO data. As a high-risk equity crowdfunding portal subject to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615), the company must carry out beneficial ownership verification of every investor, shareholder, and project promoter, and such customer due diligence records and beneficial ownership information must be refreshed at least annually for continuing business relationships.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise under Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 2. The standard headline CIT rate is 25%. No statutory tax holiday applies to an equity crowdfunding portal. Preferential incentives may apply if the WFOE qualifies as a High and New Technology Enterprise (reduced 15% rate) or as a Small Low-Profit Enterprise (effective concessional rate on taxable income up to RMB 3 million). A 100% additional R&D super-deduction is available for qualifying software and platform engineering R&D expenditures, giving a total deduction of 200% of qualifying R&D costs. No patent box, free-zone, or offshore income exemption is available because the WFOE's core income-generating activities are performed within mainland China.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 - Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (A Class), filed through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax portal). The return is the principal annual CIT reconciliation return for the Chinese WFOE, accompanied by relevant schedules including A105000 (tax adjustment items), A105050 (related party transactions), A105080 (asset depreciation), A107010 (tax-exempt and deducted incomes), and the related-party transaction reporting form A109000 series.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual with quarterly provisional prepayment installments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return must be filed and settled no later than May 31 of the following calendar year after the fiscal year-end. Quarterly provisional returns are due within 15 days after each quarter-end, and the final reconciliation with any balance payable is settled upon the annual filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business revenue: gross operating revenue from portal success fees, escrow facilitation fees, listing fees, subscription commissions, and digital intermediary services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter gross revenues from both mainland and non-resident issuers if the WFOE is the service provider. Ensure VAT-exclusive amounts reconcile to the VAT return. Do not offset intercompany expenses against revenue; do not reclassify fees as a cost reimbursement merely because the HK parent issues an invoice. Any funneling of mainland crowdfunding revenue to an HK entity without commensurate mainland activity is a permanent establishment red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating cost: direct platform technology costs, KYC verification, customer support, escrow settlement costs, and cloud infrastructure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany cloud, software, or technology-service costs paid to the HK parent must be supported by a charge-sharing agreement, actual service evidence, and an arm’s-length fee benchmark. Allocate costs on a functional analysis consistent with the OECD Guidelines. Unsubstantiated cost-plus payments to the HK parent are non-deductible and trigger transfer pricing adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and surcharges: urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, stamp tax, property tax, vehicle tax, and other creditable business taxes recognized in the profit or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not include CIT, late-payment surcharges, tax penalties, or non-deductible VAT borne on entertainment expenses. Only taxes actually paid and properly accrued are deductible. Cross-border payments subject to withholding tax must be grossed-up correctly and must not be claimed as a deductible tax here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses: marketing, digital advertising, referral incentives, listing promotion, and investor-acquisition expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Promotional spend connected with overseas issuer leads or HK parent marketing campaigns must be recharged to the WFOE only where the WFOE receives the economic benefit and controls the campaign. Business entertainment expenses exceeding the statutory deduction ceiling must be added back in Line 14. No deduction is available for unlawful rebates or inducements to unlicensed securities distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative expenses: office rental, administrative salaries, legal and professional fees, board fees, and general management overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid by a Chinese WFOE to its foreign parent or HK parent are not deductible as a matter of Chinese tax law, regardless of contract terms. Professional fees must be supported with invoices from licensed providers. Payments to directors resident in Hong Kong are deductible only if the services are actually performed for the WFOE, employment substance exists, and relevant individual income tax reporting is satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses: interest expense, bank charges, exchange losses, and financing costs on loans, debentures, or use of credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to the HK parent or any non-resident related lender is subject to thin capitalization limitations: for a non-financial enterprise, deductible related-party debt cannot exceed 2:1 debt-to-equity unless the taxpayer proves arm’s-length commercial capacity. Excess interest is non-deductible and must be added back. Interest paid on an actual cross-border loan must be supported by a written loan agreement, an arm’s-length rate, and loan registration where required. Outbound interest WHT at 10% statutory or 7% under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA must be withheld on gross interest paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Asset impairment losses: impairment of receivables, intangible assets, goodwill, and other non-financial assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accrual-basis impairment provisions are generally not deductible until the loss is actually realized and evidenced. Receivables from the HK parent or affiliated issuers are deductible only if a genuine commercial bad-debt event occurs and arm’s-length collection procedures are demonstrated. Related-party debt that is waived to subsidize the HK parent will be treated as a non-deductible contribution or dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fair value changes: gains or losses on financial instruments measured at fair value under PRC accounting standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An equity crowdfunding portal typically holds escrow and settlement obligations that are not speculative financial assets. If fair value gains arise on investments held by the WFOE, tax recognition may follow realization rules unless the instrument qualifies under specific taxation provisions. Non-resident investor assets held in escrow are not income of the WFOE and must be excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Investment income: dividends, interest on investments, and income from associates or joint ventures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends received from a Chinese resident investee company are tax-exempt for the WFOE under Article 26 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law only if they are non-public-traded shares or the holding period exceeds 12 months for listed shares. Dividends from a HK investee are generally taxable in China, with a foreign tax credit available if underlying Hong Kong profits tax was paid. Ensure that investment income from special-mentioned platforms is not incorrectly excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit: the accounting profit from ordinary activities after operating costs, expenses, impairment, fair value gains, and investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the book operating profit before non-operating items. The figure must agree with the audited financial statements of the WFOE. Cross-border recharge adjustments and transfer pricing corrections must be reflected at the adjustment stages, not by altering this book figure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income: government grants, debt forgiveness, liquidated damages, rewards, and miscellaneous income outside ordinary operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Government grants are generally taxable unless they qualify for specific exemption. Debt forgiveness from the HK parent or a shareholder in relation to loans that are deemed equity may be treated as a capital contribution and not taxable, but this requires strict legal restructuring evidence. Any waiver of intercompany debt with no equity intent is taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating expenditure: donations, penalties, fines, losses from non-operating activities, and asset disposals outside normal operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax penalties, late-payment surcharges, illegal fines, and payments to unlicensed intermediaries are non-deductible and must be added back. Charitable donations are deductible only if made to qualified Chinese public welfare organizations, within 12% of annual accounting profit, and supported by legally recognized receipts. Amounts paid to HK shell entities for purported sponsorship or settlement services are not deductible unless genuine and business-related.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total profit: accounting profit before income tax, equal to Line 10 plus Line 11 minus Line 12.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This line must equal the profit before tax in the WFOE’s statutory financial statements. It forms the starting point for all tax adjustments. If the WFOE has a HK parent with no mainland substance, the tax authority may deem the entire group’s business to be a mainland PE and assess additional income beyond the WFOE’s book profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income increases: adjustments that increase accounting profit to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible management fees paid to HK parent, excessive intercompany interest, transfer pricing undercharges, entertainment expenses above the cap, tax penalties, and expenses without valid invoices. If the WFOE undercharged the HK parent for technology or data services, the tax authority will make a special tax investigation adjustment and increase Line 14. Related-party transaction schedules must be fully disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income decreases: adjustments that reduce taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct qualifying R&D super-deduction amounts, tax-exempt dividend income, and eligible loss carryforwards from prior years. Foreign tax credits are not entered in line 15 but are applied in the credit line after tax is computed. Cross-border transfer pricing adjustments that reduce taxable income are permitted only if supported by a robust OECD-compliant TP documentation file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income used to offset domestic losses: tax loss offset from foreign branch or foreign-investment losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a WFOE with a Hong Kong or foreign subsidiary, foreign-source losses may be available to offset mainland taxable income only to the extent permitted by specific cross-border loss rules and only where controlled-foreign-company provisions do not reattribute income. This is not a general mechanism for mixing HK group losses with China profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward offset: use of prior-year tax losses against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may be carried forward for five years, and for qualified High and New Technology Enterprises or certain small and medium enterprises, the period may be extended to ten years. The loss carryforward must be computed using the Chinese tax loss, not the accounting loss, and must exclude portions attributable to related-party transactions that are adjusted by tax authorities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: final amount subject to CIT after all increases, decreases, and loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that when non-resident shareholders are present, the taxable income has not been depressed by non-deductible group charges or inflated royalty payments. The WFOE must file contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation if related-party transaction thresholds are exceeded. Understating taxable income through HK crowdfunding-portal arrangements may constitute tax evasion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax rate: the CIT rate applied to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the applicable statutory rate: 25% for a general WFOE, 15% for a qualified High and New Technology Enterprise, or the concessional rate for a Small Low-Profit Enterprise if the legal requirements are satisfied. The Mainland-Hong Kong DTA rate for dividends or royalties is not applied inside this line; treaty benefits are applied at the withholding stage for non-resident recipients.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed income tax payable: Line 18 multiplied by Line 19.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the preliminary CIT before tax credits and reductions. Cross-border withholding taxes paid in a foreign jurisdiction can be credited only in later lines under foreign tax credit rules, and only where the income is the same taxable income and the credit is substantiated with tax payment certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reductions and exemptions: reductions that lower the computed tax before foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the reduction from the High and New Technology Enterprise rate (from 25% to 15%) or the Small Low-Profit Enterprise concession. Do not enter domestic withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents. Do not use this line to claim treaty-based relief for HK shareholders; treaty relief occurs at the payer’s withholding stage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits: credits for income tax paid outside China on foreign-source taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Creditable amounts are limited to the Chinese tax payable on the foreign-source income computed under China’s rate. If HK profits tax has been paid by a HK parent, that tax is not automatically creditable in the WFOE unless the WFOE itself has foreign-source income and qualifying foreign tax certificates. A non-resident parent’s HK taxes cannot reduce WFOE’s CIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Actual income tax payable: Line 20 minus Line 21 minus Line 22.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the final mainland CIT liability of the WFOE for the year. Dividends distributed from after-tax profit to the HK parent are not deductible and do not reduce this amount. The WFOE must ensure this liability is paid before distributing dividends; otherwise, dividends are considered paid out of untaxed profits and the entire amount may be subject to further tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepaid income tax: the quarterly provisional CIT amounts already paid by the WFOE during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must have made quarterly advances based on actual profit or prior-year benchmark. If the WFOE made insufficient prepayments due to artificial HK holding-structure losses, the tax authority may impose late-payment interest from the date each installment was due. Prepayments made by the WFOE cannot be credited against WHT obligations of the HK shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable or refundable balance: Line 23 minus Line 24.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance must be paid by May 31. Any overpayment can be refunded or applied as a credit under tax authority approval. A refund request must be filed before the limitation period expires. If the balance is nil because dividends were incorrectly deducted as expenses, the correction will increase the tax due and expose the WFOE to penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual CIT return on time is subject to a late-filing fine of up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 if issued after a tax authority demand. Late payment of CIT incurs a daily surcharge of 0.05% on the overdue amount from the due date. Understating taxable income due to false or incomplete related-party disclosures is subject to a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. Criminal tax evasion under Article 201 of the Criminal Law applies where the amount evaded exceeds RMB 50,000 and constitutes more than 10% of the tax due, carrying imprisonment for up to three years for minor evasion and from three to seven years for serious evasion; where forged or fraudulent tax invoices are involved, longer sentences and asset confiscation may apply. The legal representative may also be placed on the tax authorities’ serious untrustworthy list and prohibited from leaving mainland China.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory dividend withholding tax under Article 37 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and Article 3 of the Implementation Regulations for dividends distributed by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise shareholder. The rate is reduced to 5% under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement if the Hong Kong resident shareholder is the beneficial owner of the dividend and holds at least 25% of the WFOE’s shares. Where treaty benefits are denied, statutory 10% withholding tax applies to gross dividends and no deduction is available to the WFOE for the distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the 5% DTA dividend rate, the Hong Kong shareholder must file a treaty-benefit application through the WFOE’s withholding-agent procedures before the dividend payment is made. The WFOE must submit to the competent Chinese tax authority: (1) a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate issued by the Inland Revenue Department covering the year in which the dividend is paid; (2) a signed declaration of beneficial ownership confirming the HK shareholder owns and receives the dividend for its own account; (3) an organizational chart and certificate of shareholding demonstrating direct ownership of at least 25% of the WFOE; (4) audited financial statements and payroll records of the HK parent demonstrating substantive business activities in Hong Kong, including board meetings, decision-making, office premises, and staff; and (5) the original or certified copies of all underlying dividend resolution, escrow settlement, and group agreements. The application is processed through the e-Tax portal under the procedures for non-resident enterprises claiming tax treaty benefits as set out in SAT Announcement 2015 No. 60. The Chinese tax authority may require the WFOE to withhold at the 10% rate pending approval, and if the beneficial-ownership test fails due to shell-company indicators, the 10% WHT will apply retroactively together with late-payment interest and penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by the WFOE to a non-resident for the use of or right to use intellectual property such as software, trademarks, patents, or algorithms are subject to a statutory 10% withholding tax on the gross amount under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. Under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA, royalties are generally subject to a reduced rate of 5% where the Hong Kong resident is the beneficial owner. Interest paid by the WFOE to a non-resident related lender is subject to a statutory 10% withholding tax on gross interest; the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA reduces the maximum rate to 7% for interest arising in mainland China and beneficially owned by a Hong Kong resident. Treaty relief for interest requires the same TRC and beneficial-ownership certification, plus a genuine written loan agreement and normal commercial terms. Royalties and interest are also subject to VAT at 6% on the taxable services from overseas suppliers under cross-border deemed sale rules, with the WFOE generally responsible for VAT withholding and remittance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: China requires a Local File to be prepared where annual related-party transactions meet any of these thresholds: tangible asset transfers above RMB 200 million; transfers or use of intangible property above RMB 100 million; financial asset transactions above RMB 100 million; or other related-party transactions above RMB 40 million. A Master File is required where the aggregate amount of related-party transactions in the year exceeds RMB 1 billion. The WFOE must also file the annual related-party transaction reporting form A109000 with its annual CIT return whenever any related-party transaction occurs, irrespective of value.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The economic-substance doctrine under Chinese law is embodied in the general anti-abuse rule of Article 120 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law, the specialty anti-avoidance rules for controlled foreign companies, thin capitalization, and the beneficial-ownership requirements of the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA. For an equity crowdfunding portal, Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) include platform development, investor onboarding, issue listing, operational risk management, escrow administration, and compliance decisions surrounding securities offerings. Where the WFOE performs those CIGA in mainland China while the HK parent provides only nominee services or title to the platform code, the HK entity will be disregarded for Chinese tax purposes, and the income will be reattributed to the WFOE or to a mainland permanent establishment. The Hong Kong parent must substantiate its own decision-making, staff, premises, and assumption of risk in Hong Kong to satisfy economic-substance requirements and to qualify for treaty benefits. A paper-thin HK holding company that merely invoices the WFOE for services or receives dividends without functional substance is a fatal treaty-shopping structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion through transfer-pricing manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE signs a non-arm’s-length licensing and group-service agreement with its Hong Kong parent under which the WFOE remits 90% of crowdfunding success fees as a royalty to the HK parent, while all key employees, servers, users, business decisions, and compliance functions remain in mainland China. No contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation is prepared, the contractual allocation does not match the actual functions, assets, and risks, and the WFOE reports zero or artificially low taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may apply the transfer-pricing adjustment rules under Articles 41 and 123 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and Articles 112-115 of the Implementation Regulations, re-imputing the full arm’s-length profit to the WFOE, denying the management fee deduction, reassessing CIT at 25% on the adjusted profit, and imposing a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day. A penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax applies under Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law. If the amount of tax evaded exceeds RMB 50,000 and accounts for more than 10% of the tax due, Criminal Law Article 201 imposes imprisonment for up to three years for minor cases and three to seven years for serious cases, plus fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the veil-piercing doctrine of the PRC Company Law, directors and the legal representative who caused the WFOE to underpay CIT and divert profits to the HK parent may be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and penalties where they abused corporate separation or participated in fraud. Tax authorities may place the legal representative on the serious tax untrustworthiness blacklist, impose a travel ban preventing departure from mainland China, restrict high-consumption activities, and freeze personal assets. Upon criminal conviction for tax evasion, directors face imprisonment sentences of three to seven years, and confiscation of personal property derived from the evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell-company structure and fraudulent claim of treaty benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong parent exists only at a registered address with no employees, no real office, no trading activity, and no board meetings in Hong Kong. The WFOE claims the reduced 5% dividend withholding tax rate under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA and represents that the HK parent is the beneficial owner of dividends, royalties, and interest, while in fact the HK parent is a conduit serving the ultimate mainland offshore investor. This is a treaty-shopping arrangement designed to avoid Chinese withholding tax and to avoid the establishment of a permanent establishment in mainland China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 120 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and the special tax collection measures applicable to treaty benefits, the tax authority may deny the treaty-claim, apply the general anti-abuse rule, disregard the existence of the HK parent, recharacterize the payments as taxable dividends or service revenue, and assess 25% CIT on the underlying profit plus 10% withholding tax on outbound distributions. The taxpayer will owe late-payment interest from the original due date and a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. Where forged Tax Residency Certificates or false beneficial-ownership declarations are used, the matter is treated as tax fraud under Criminal Law Article 201, and the relevant legal documents are reported to Hong Kong authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who deliberately organized the HK shell, signed false beneficial-ownership declarations, or directed dividend payments to the HK conduit are personally exposed to civil liability for the unpaid taxes and interest through corporate-veil piercing. The legal representative is subject to exit restrictions and blacklisting by the Chinese tax authorities, and may be placed on the cross-border travel-ban list. If the fraudulent treaty claim is criminalized, imprisonment of three to seven years is possible, together with confiscation of bank accounts and shares held in the HK shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed equity crowdfunding and anti-money-laundering non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE operates an equity crowdfunding portal that accepts subscriptions from non-accredited mainland investors, pools investor funds into an escrow bank account, issues success fees, and facilitates the purchase of startup equity without holding a securities-related license from the China Securities Regulatory Commission or any qualified equity-crowdfunding license. The portal also fails to perform customer due diligence, beneficial-ownership screening, transaction monitoring, and suspicious-transaction reporting required for a high-risk online payment intermediary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed securities intermediary operation is an illegal business operation under Criminal Law Article 225 and may also constitute an illegal public offering or illegal securities business under the PRC Securities Law. Operating without the required license is punishable by confiscation of illegal income and fines up to five times the illegal turnover; serious criminal cases carry imprisonment from five to ten years with fines and asset confiscation. Under the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law, failure to meet AML obligations subjects the institution to fines ranging from RMB 1 million to RMB 5 million and the responsible directors and officers to fines from RMB 50,000 to RMB 500,000, plus removal from office and disqualification from the financial sector.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the legal representative who knowingly operated an unlicensed crowdfunding portal and laundered investor funds through the escrow account are personally liable for investor losses through tort and fraudulent-trading doctrines. The Chinese regulator may ban them from serving as directors of any licensed financial, securities, or payment entity, blacklist them, freeze their personal bank accounts, and prohibit them from leaving the country. Criminal conviction for illegal business operation is punishable by five to ten years’ imprisonment in serious cases; AML violations may add separate imprisonment terms and monetary fines, with personal restitution ordered for diverted investor funds.
